about: Car Salesman Slaps Roof of Car is a drawing of a smiling salesman in a dark suit presenting a silver car to a thoughtful customer who rubs his chin. The joke is the sales pitch: the salesman slaps the roof and boasts that "this bad boy" holds an absurd amount of something. The thing being sold does not have to be a car at all; the format turns any object, app, person or idea into a vehicle that can "fit" a ridiculous quantity of something, usually something bad that the seller is proud of anyway.
origin: The phrasing started as a 2014 tweet imagining a salesman bragging that a car could fit an enormous amount of spaghetti. The drawn salesman and buyer became the standard picture for the joke during the 2017-2018 wave of the meme.
usage:
Top box: "*slaps roof of*" plus the thing being sold, or just "this bad boy can fit". Bottom box: the contents, phrased as "so much X in it", where X is the surprising contents. The joke depends on the cheerful sales tone clashing with what is being bragged about.

Good targets are products stuffed with ads, codebases full of bugs, schedules crammed with meetings, or anything that holds a lot of the wrong stuff. Keep the pitch voice: "bad boy", "so much", and the slap. Short second lines read best under the drawing.
ideas: this bad boy can fit so many ads in it
this bad boy can fit so many bugs in it
this bad boy can fit so many meetings in it
this bad boy can fit so much drama in it
this bad boy can fit so many unfinished assignments
this bad boy can fit so many cancelled shows in it
aka: This Bad Boy Can Fit So Much
